text:
Alice M: Heads up — I noticed a regression on the 4xA100 nightly after the kernel-selector tweak (PR #842). Latency p50 for the long-sequence chat workload jumped ~12% and p99 spiked more. Captured an nsys run and a perfetto trace: https://perfetto.link/trace/xyz789 :eyes:

Ben R: Hmm. Did you include NCCL and NVTX traces? That usually helps show overlap.

Alice M: Yep, nsys with --trace=nvtx,nccl,cuda,osrt,cupti. Link above includes the timeline. Key symptom: attention kernels (attention_kernel_v2) are taking ~18–22ms each (used to be ~12–14ms) and we also see sustained NCCL all-reduce activity overlapping those kernels, increasing pipeline stalls.

Carla S: Can you paste the CLI you used? I'll run the same capture locally.

Alice M: Sure — command I used:
```
nsys profile --output=run_1803456789 --trace=cuda,nccl,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none --force-overwrite -- sleep 60
```
Captured with model config: batch=8 global_batch=32 tp=1 pp=4 kv_cache=true, new-kernel-selector=enabled

Ben R: Looking at the perfetto flame: the all-reduce windows are longer and start earlier in the pipeline stage. That suggests the runtime is choosing a kernel variant that increases per-step compute time but also shifts the timing such that more gradients/activations participate in overlapping collectives. Possibly unintended interaction between batching heuristic and kernel latencies.

Dmitri K: Pasting a small excerpt from the NCCL timeline (nsys summary):
```
NCCL op: allReduce size=128MB start=120ms end=152ms duration=32.0ms
NCCL op: allReduce size=64MB start=220ms end=248ms duration=28.0ms
CUDA kernel: attention_kernel_v2 start=115ms end=137ms duration=22.0ms
CUDA kernel: cutlass_gemm_fused start=140ms end=150ms duration=10.0ms
```
The overlapping windows look like attention_kernel_v2 now spans into where we used to have a short GEMM+comm gap.

Eva L: My guess — the new selector picked an attention kernel optimized for larger micro-batches (it fuses more ops), which increases single-step compute but reduces launches. For our multi-GPU pipeline, that shift increases overlap with NCCL because the communication was scheduled assuming the shorter kernel. In other words, kernel selection changed the schedule shape.

Ben R: Agreed. Also saw increased host<->device memcpy before KV handshake in the trace. KV cache handshake timings: prefetch copy ~1.8ms -> used to be ~0.6ms. If handshake pushed later, it could backpressure and change the op ordering.

Carla S: Reproduced locally. When I force the selector to choose legacy_attention via env var REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy, the p50 returns to baseline and the NCCL windows shrink. Quick numbers from micro-run (8iters):
- new selector: p50=185ms p99=420ms
- legacy: p50=165ms p99=300ms

Dmitri K: Interesting. Can we diff the NVTX region boundaries? If the fusion removed an NVTX marker, the scheduler heuristics that split comms might not trigger. I can run a perfetto with thread slices highlighted.

Alice M: I also noticed the batching heuristic allowed global_batch to combine into fewer larger micro-batches after the change. It seems the selector returned a slightly higher preferred_micro_batch_size which caused more tokens to be processed per step.

Eva L: Actionable experiments:
1) Re-run nsys with explicit nvtx annotations from runtime (force markers around KV handshake, attention entry/exit).
2) Compare kernel-level durations (attention variants, fused-gemm) across selector=legacy vs selector=new.
3) Run a synthetic all-reduce-only NCCL microbenchmark to ensure no regression in raw NCCL perf.
4) Try setting REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_MICROBATCH= (lower) to see if splitting micro-batches reduces overlap.

Ben R: I'll take 1&2. Dmitri can you run 3? Carla can validate 4 on CI?

perf-bot: nightly-run/1803456000 completed: model-inference-bench (4xA100). Regression alert triggered: end-to-end p50 +11.6% vs baseline. Link: https://ci.redwood/bench/1803456000

Dmitri K: NCCL microbench results (quick run): all-reduce 128MB throughput consistent with baseline, latency unchanged ~30ms. So NCCL itself looks fine — it's the timing overlap that's changed.

Carla S: CI run with REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_MICROBATCH=2 dropped p50 by ~6% and p99 by ~20% compared to new-selector default. So batching change mitigates the effect but doesn't fully recover baseline.

Alice M: Good to know. That means two levers: kernel choice and batching heuristic. My preferred short-term fix is to gate the new selector behind a rollout flag per-customer and revert for the general pool until we have a selector that is comm-aware.

Ben R: Long-term: update kernel selector cost model to include network overlap penalty. It should estimate how increasing compute latency for a kernel variant affects downstream NCCL windows using a simple model (critical path). Also, KV cache handshake cost needs to be included (host memcpy variance).

Eva L: Also add a perf test in the CI which runs a multi-GPU pipeline scenario that specifically measures comm+compute overlap. That'll catch regressions faster.

Dmitri K: I'll upload annotated perfetto slices and NVTX diff later today. Look for link in this thread.

Alice M: Thanks team. Summary of immediate next steps I recorded in the issue: revert selector rollout flag, add selector CI test, tune batcher default to safer split, add NVTX markers for KV handshake. Assigning owners: Ben (timeline diffs + selector model change), Carla (batcher CI test + rollout), Dmitri (NCCL microbench + perfetto slices), Eva (KV handshake instrumentation).

Ben R: 👍 I'll open a PR to add the comm-aware term to the cost function and include a flag to disable it for the moment.

perf-bot: issue-897 updated: regression triage in progress (labels: perf, infra).

Alice M: Thanks. If anyone captures more traces, drop links here.
